fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 2019-8343 (passed June 25, 2019, administered by Mattagami Region Conservation Authority; https://mattagamiregion.ca/wp-content/uploads/2020/01/2019-8343-Site-Alteration-By-Law.pdf) s. 3.4 verbatim exempts BOTH placement and removal of topsoil for Normal Farm Practices: 'The provisions of this by-law, with respect to the requirement to obtain a Site Alteration Permit as described in the Site Alteration Guidelines, do not apply to the placement and/or removal of topsoil as an incidental part of a normal agricultural practices including, sod farming, greenhouse operations and nurseries for horticultural products' (s. 3.1.6 also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. For non-exempt sites, the City of Timmins Site Alteration Fee Schedule (eff. Jan 1, 2020; published in Site Alteration Guideline 2022 Table A p. 4, active Application Form, and live on MRCA Fees page https://mattagamiregion.ca/fees/) charges flat fees ($0/m³): Category 1 (Grade Alteration >0.15 m, no import/export) = $100 (<500 m³) or $400 (≥500 m³); Category 2 (Small Site Alteration, import/export <500 m³) = $200.00; Category 3 (Large Site Alteration, import/export ≥500 m³) = $400.00; Permit Renewal = $50.00; Unpermitted work = double permit fee (2×). No geographic out-of-municipality fill ban.

fields.fee_formula_notes: Full signed PDF of Site Alteration By-law No. 2025-033 (passed May 12, 2025; retrieved from Amherstburg public SharePoint Records Repository) s. 3.1(k) exempts 'Site Alterations incidental to a Normal Farm Practice that is legally established under the Town's Zoning By-law, including the application of Topsoil for spreading over Agricultural Property provided that the Existing Grade of the Property is not increased by more than 200 millimetres at any given point. This exception is only available to those Owners or Properties that have an active registration as a "farming business" as defined in the Farm Registration and Farms Organization Funding Act ("FRFOFA"), and are in good standing under the FRFOFA' ($0; also exempts NFP topsoil removal s. 3.1(c) and Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act s. 3.1(i)). CAVEAT: Exemption has no m³ volume cap (200 mm over a typical 20-acre field = 16,000 m³), but DOES require active FBRN/FRFOFA status and caps grade increase at ≤200 mm (and s. 1.1(l) Fill definition includes Topsoil, Sod, and Compost). Non-exempt or >200 mm projects pay 2026 User Fee By-law No. 2025-085 Sched F (tax exempt, non-refundable + actual costs + $5,000 min deposit): Minor (<350 m³, excl. liquid) = $511.00; Large (>350 m³, excl. liquid) = $1,021.00; Large (>10,000 m³ or liquid, requiring Council public meeting under s. 4.4 & RPRA Excess Soil Registry filing) = $2,041.00. No out-of-municipality fill ban (O. Reg. 406/19 & 153/04 source-site quality rules apply).

fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 1664-16 (amended by 2120-20 & 2124-20; https://www.haldimandcounty.ca/government-administration/by-laws-and-policies/by-law-directory/site-alteration-by-law/) s. 11(c) verbatim states: 'A Permit is not required for: ... c. Jan 1, 2026, repealing 2560/24; Schedule C — Roads Operations, corroborated on 2026 Permit Application https://www.haldimandcounty.ca/media/t23hkehj/bme-site-alteration-permit-application-25-12.pdf) sets a flat Site Alteration Permit fee of $271.00 non-refundable (2025: $263.00; $0/m³).

fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 2020-44 (visually verified 33-page scanned PDF: https://media-001-ca.cdn.govstack.com/grimsbylibrary-005-ca/media/1kmlue3y/2020-044-002-fill.pdf) s. 15(a)(i) verbatim exempts 'Dumping or placing of Topsoil on a Site for improving the soil capability for agricultural purposes on Agricultural Lands as part of a Normal Farm Practice', and s. 15(m) exempts any Site Alteration determined to be a Normal Farm Practice carried on by Owners/properties with active FRFOFA/FBRN registration in good standing (s. 15(h) also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. For non-exempt sites, 2026 Consolidated Fees & Charges Schedule L – Public Works (p. 4, visually verified, HST exempt) sets flat fees ($0/m³): Standard Permit (exceeding lot-size free thresholds up to <1,000 m³: >10 m³ on ≤0.1 ha, >50 m³ on >0.1–0.2 ha, >100 m³ on >0.2–0.5 ha, >500 to <1,000 m³ on ≥0.5 ha) = $624.00; Large Permit (>1,000 m³, Council approval required) = $1,040.00; Revision = $260.00; Renewal (2 mo prior) = $520.00; Post-permit engineering/zoning review = $1,040.00; Haul route inspection = $107.00; Post-commencement surcharge = 150%; Violation site investigation = $538.00. Part V s. 6–10 bans remunerated Commercial Fill Operations but imposes no geographic origin ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Site Alteration By-law No. 2026-007 (passed Feb 24, 2026; s. 14(g) NFP Exemption & Schedule C, p. 22)
fields.security_deposit_terms: When non-exempt (By-law 2026-007 Schedule C s. 4–10): Irrevocable Letter of Credit/security of $15,000.00 (Standard Permit) or up to 5% of assessed property value (Large Site Alteration); $250.00 retained per follow-up close-out inspection.
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (By-law 2026-007 s. 46 & Schedule C s. 2): Applicant pays the entire cost of Town-retained professionals, consultants and engineers; O. Reg. 406/19 Qualified Person letter and Excess Soil documentation required (s. 20(g)–(i)).
fields.fee_formula_notes: Enacted February 24, 2026 (repealing By-law 3941-05), Site Alteration By-law No. 2026-007 s. 14(g) verbatim exempts 'Any work pursuant to Normal Farm Practice with a setback of 3.05 m (10 ft) or greater from all property lines that does not change the direction, rate or quality of runoff that results in a detrimental effect on neighbouring properties' (relaxed from 7.62 m / 25 ft under repealed 3941-05), subject to s. 15 requiring 48 hours prior written notice to the Director ($0 fee, no volume cap). Schedule F clarifies NFP excludes tile drains (separately exempt under s. 14(f) with 7-day notice & tile plan to Drainage Superintendent), ditches, ponds, berms, and removal of topsoil/aggregate for sale, exchange or disposition. For non-exempt sites, Schedule C (p. 22, 6-month permit; no $/m³ rate) sets: Standard Site Alteration Permit = $750.00 flat; Large Site Alteration Permit (>1,000 m³ fill placed or excess soil removed, OR >50 m³/ha, OR >500 m³ stockpiled >6 mo, OR >1 m grade change; requires Public Information Centre) = $1,500.00 + $25.00/ha (or part thereof) over 5 ha; 6-month extension = 50% of initial fee. General minor exemption <20 m³/ha & <0.2 m grade change (s. 8). Off-site fill is permitted with pit/depot purchase order or O. Reg. 406/19 QP letter (s. 20(g)); hydro-excavation/liquid soil requires Council approval (s. 18).

fields.fees_bylaw_name: 2026 User Fees and Charges Guide (Public Works — Engineering Fees, p. 59) & Environmental Protection By-law No. 3357 (2013) s. 3(h)
fields.security_deposit_terms: None published in Environmental Protection By-law No. 3357 (2013) (as amended by By-laws 4111(2019) & 4222(2020)) or 2026 Engineering Fees (p. 59).
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (By-law 3357 (2013) s. 8(a)): Town may retain a third-party geotechnical/environmental consultant to inspect and analyze fill with costs charged to contravening person if non-compliant; 2026 User Fees Guide p. 24 lists Special Studies EIS peer review fees ($1,530–$4,045).
fields.fee_formula_notes: Environmental Protection By-law No. 3357 (2013) (https://www.bylawappdb-pelham.ca/uploads/Bylaws/Scans/3415_folder/bylawId_3415/bylaw_text_folder/3357_2013.pdf) s. 3(h) verbatim exempts Normal Farm Practice: 'This by-law shall not apply to: ... h. activities or matters which are an incidental part of a Normal Farm Practice including such removal as an incidental part of sod-farming, greenhouse operations, and nurseries for horticultural purposes; however this exemption does not include, and this by-law applies to, the removal of topsoil for sale, exchange or other disposition' (s. 3(g) also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. IMPORTANT ORIGIN RESTRICTION: Amending By-law No. 4222(2020) (visually verified) added s. 5(a) strictly prohibiting fill originating outside Niagara Region or of undetermined origin ('No person shall import, or otherwise bring, any fill into the Town where the origin of the material is located outside of the geographic area of the Niagara Region or where the origin of the material is undetermined'), while permitting intra-Niagara fill (modeled as 'Restricted'). Amending By-law No. 4111(2019) added s. 8(b) requiring a Fill Questionnaire & written Town approval prior to non-exempt fill placement (s. 7 caps non-NFP fill on Productive Agricultural Lands at <2,000 m³ Table 1 soil). For non-exempt sites, 2026 User Fees and Charges Guide (Public Works — Engineering Fees, p. 59) sets: Minor Site Alteration Permit = $670.00 (2025: $660); Site Alteration Permit (Residential 10 Units or Less) = $1,180.00 (2025: $1,156); Grading Review = $420.00 ($0/m³).

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Site Alteration By-law No. 17-2021 (s. 15(a)(i)/(m) NFP Exemption & Schedule B; active in 2026)
fields.security_deposit_terms: When non-exempt (By-law 17-2021 Schedule B Sec B): Permits >1,000 m³ require financial security at the Director's discretion, minimum $1,000.00 (cash only if <$50,000; irrevocable LOC if ≥$50,000); $5M CGL insurance required (s. 17(e)).
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (By-law 17-2021 s. 36 & Permit Application Form p. 5): All City costs for retained legal, engineering and technical consultants are charged back to the Owner (collectible via property tax roll).
fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 17-2021 (https://media-003-ca.cdn.govstack.com/thorold-ca/media/o4nfvx3b/by-law-no-17-2021-site-alteration.pdf) s. 15(a)(i) exempts dumping or placing Topsoil to improve agricultural soil capability on Agricultural Lands as part of a Normal Farm Practice, and s. 15(m) exempts any Site Alteration determined to be a Normal Farm Practice carried out by an active FBRN-registered Owner/property in good standing (s. 15(h) also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. Full inspection of Thorold's 57-page 2026 Consolidated Fees and Charges By-law No. 14-2026 (consolidated April 14, 2026) confirms Site Alteration fees are not listed there, leaving Schedule B of By-law 17-2021 (published in active Application & Permit Forms PDF, p. 9) in force: Standard Permit (>lot-size free thresholds up to <1,000 m³) = $500.00 flat; Large Permit (>1,000 m³, Council approval required) = $1,000.00 flat ($0/m³); Renewal = $250/$500; Post-permit review = $1,000; Haul route inspection = $100 each; Post-commencement = 150%; Violation site investigation = 100% of application fee. s. 10 bans remunerated Commercial Fill Operations with no geographic origin ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: 2026 General Fees & Charges By-law No. 044-2025 (Schedule A — Public Works, p. 8) & Site Alteration By-law No. 025-2022 s. 6.1(a)(i)/(n)
fields.security_deposit_terms: When non-exempt (2026 By-law 044-2025 Schedule A p. 8 & By-law 025-2022 s. 9.3): Site Alteration Road Damage Deposit = $10,864.00 (2026; up from $10,609 in 2025 and $10,000 in 2022 Sched C), plus additional Site Alteration Agreement security (>1,000 m³); $2M CGL insurance (s. 7.1(e) as amended by By-law 016-2023).
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (By-law 025-2022 s. 10.6, s. 12.3 & s. 10.1(j)): Township legal, engineering and technical consultant costs plus inspection testing/sampling costs are charged back to Owner; QP/P.Eng. clean-fill report required.
fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 025-2022 (https://www.wainfleet.ca/sites/24/files/2024-06/BL025-2022-Site-Alteration.pdf; amended by By-law 016-2023 reducing CGL insurance from $5M to $2M) s. 6.1(a)(i) exempts dumping or placing Topsoil for improving soil capability on Agricultural Lands as part of a Normal Farm Practice, and s. 6.1(n) exempts any NFP Site Alteration by an active FRFOFA/FBRN-registered Owner in good standing (s. 6.1(i) also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. For non-exempt sites, 2026 General Fees & Charges By-law No. 044-2025 (Schedule A — Public Works, p. 8 / PDF p. 10, eff. Jan 1, 2026, HST exempt) sets tiered flat fees ($0/m³): <500 m³ = $538.00 (2025: $525); 500–1,000 m³ = $1,086.00 (2025: $1,061); 1,000 m³+ (Council approval required) = $1,629.00 (2025: $1,591). General minor free thresholds under s. 6.2 are ≤10 m³/yr (≤1 ha) or ≤50 m³/yr (≥1 ha) with written notice. s. 5.6 bans remunerated Commercial Fill Operations with no geographic origin ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: 2026 Building and By-law Fees and Charges & Site Alteration By-law No. 2012-10 (s. 2(c)(ix) & Schedule A, p. 16)
fields.security_deposit_terms: When non-exempt (By-law 2012-10 s. 3(c) & s. 4(b)): Cash, cheque, or irrevocable bank Letter of Credit in an amount approved by the Township (if required), released upon compliance / P.Eng. certification.
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (By-law 2012-10 s. 4(c) & s. 3(e)): Township may engage legal, engineering, hydrology, environmental, arborist or landscape consultants deemed necessary by the Chief Building Official and charge all costs back to the applicant; EIS required in Environmental Protection areas.
fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 2012-10 (https://www.hamiltontownship.ca/media/fo5maqch/by-law-2012-10-site-alteration.pdf) s. 2(c)(ix) verbatim exempts agricultural fill placement: 'The provisions of subsection (a) of this section do not apply in those areas of the Township where: ... ix. fill is dumped or placed on lands zoned Permanent Agriculture and Marginal Agriculture where there is an alteration to the grade of land as an incidental part of a commonly accepted agricultural practice' (s. 2(c)(xvii) also exempts Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act) -> $0 with no volume cap. Note: s. 2(h)(v) prohibits site alteration in Oak Ridges Moraine Natural Core Areas, Natural Linkage Areas, High Aquifer Vulnerability Areas, or Landform Conservation Areas unless tied to a building permit or development agreement. For non-exempt sites, the Township's 2026 Building and By-law Fees and Charges schedule and By-law 2012-10 Schedule A (p. 16) charge an area-based fee of $100.00 + $50.00 per hectare (or part hectare) up to an overall maximum fee of $500.00 (same for renewals; not $/m³). s. 2(a) prohibits remunerated Commercial Fill Operations with no geographic origin ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Site Alteration By-law No. 2024-448 (s. 2(2)(a) NFP Exemption; active 2026 rule-based framework with no general permit fee)
fields.security_deposit_terms: None — Ottawa's Site Alteration By-law No. 2024-448 uses a rule-based compliance framework rather than a municipal permit or performance security deposit system.
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt work is proposed in or within 30 m of Schedule B significant natural areas, prior City approval is required and an Environmental Impact Study (EIS) may be required at the owner's expense.
fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 2024-448 (enacted Oct 16, 2024, eff. Oct 30, 2024, repealing 2018-164; official page: https://ottawa.ca/en/living-ottawa/laws-licences-and-permits/laws/laws-z/site-alteration-law-no-2024-448; official 7-page City guide: https://documents.ottawa.ca/sites/default/files/site_alter_bylaw_en.pdf) s. 2(2)(a) verbatim permits/exempts 'Site Alteration that is incidental to a Normal Farm Practice carried out by an Agricultural Operation, including, but not limited to, sod-farming, greenhouse operations, nurseries, field and forage crop or livestock production, but not including the removal of Topsoil or peat for sale, exchange or other disposition' ($0, no volume cap, no prior City notification or approval required for NFP). Even for non-agricultural properties, Ottawa intentionally operates a rule-based compliance framework with NO general site alteration permit or permit fee ($0 base, $0/m³); prior City approval is triggered only within 30 m of Schedule B significant natural areas. Baseline clean fill (O. Reg. 406/19), drainage, and erosion/sediment control rules apply. An April 2026 Council amendment requires owners/operators of excess soil reuse sites or registered projects in Ottawa to email the City and Ward Councillor within 5 days of filing on the provincial RPRA Excess Soil Registry. No geographic out-of-municipality fill ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Fees By-law No. 11-09 (Consolidated Nov 4, 2026 — No Site Alteration Fee Listed) & Site Alteration By-law No. 49-03 (ss. 3.1(g), 3.2, 4.1)
fields.security_deposit_terms: None for agricultural land / NFP exempt farms; where permit applies (Environmental Protection Area or Draft Plan of Subdivision only), agreement may require security in an amount satisfactory to Township (By-law 49-03 ss. 6.1(d), 6.2(f))
fields.peer_review_recovery: None for agricultural land / NFP exempt farms; where permit applies, major activities may require applicant-submitted report from qualified engineer, biologist and/or ecologist (By-law 49-03 Sched A Item 11); Fees By-law 11-09 Sched A recovers external municipal engineering/planning services at third-party billing + 5% admin fee
fields.fee_formula_notes: DOUBLE AGRICULTURAL EXEMPTION VERIFIED: Active Site Alteration (Soil) By-law No. 49-03 (passed Sept 30, 2003; https://www.zorra.ca/assets/documents/49-03-Site-Alteration-By-law.pdf, verified current on zorra.ca/our-township/by-laws-and-policies/) (1) restricts permitting geographically under s. 4.1 strictly to 'an Environmental Protection Area or on any land that is subject to a Draft Plan of Subdivision' (ordinary farmland is unregulated), AND (2) explicitly states in s. 3.2: 'This by-law does not apply to normal agricultural practices including the ploughing of land associated with the planting, cultivation or harvesting of agricultural crops or to the removal of topsoil as an incidental part of a normal agricultural practice...' ($0; plus s. 3.1(g) Drainage Act / Tile Drainage Act). Consolidated Fees By-law No. 11-09 (consolidated Nov 4, 2026, Schedules A–G, 14 pp.) publishes no Site Alteration Permit fee line item (only a 15% admin fee, min $80.00, on default remedial work orders under By-law 49-03 s. 8.9). No out-of-municipality fill ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Site Alteration By-law No. 41-2010 (s. 3, s. 4(e)–(f) & Schedule B) & 2026 User Fees By-law No. 25-2026 (pp. 10–11)
fields.security_deposit_terms: When non-exempt Site Plan Agreement applies under By-law 41-2010 s. 2 (2026 User Fees By-law 25-2026 pp. 10–11): Minor Site Plan Agreement Deposit = $2,000.00; Major Site Plan Agreement Deposit = $7,000.00.
fields.peer_review_recovery: When non-exempt (2026 User Fees By-law 25-2026 p. 11 Note *****): All peer review and associated administrative costs are borne by the Applicant.
fields.fee_formula_notes: Site Alteration By-law No. 41-2010 (passed Oct 12, 2010; https://irp-cdn.multiscreensite.com/20e551fd/files/uploaded/Bylaw-Site_Alteration.pdf) provides a DOUBLE agricultural exemption ($0, no volume cap): (1) s. 3 & Schedule B strictly limit the entire by-law to Flood Plain (FP) Zones, Wetlands, and lands below Regulatory Flood Elevations — standard upland farmland is completely unregulated; AND (2) even inside Schedule B, s. 4(e) exempts incidental NFP topsoil removal (excl. sale) and s. 4(f) verbatim exempts 'Any work pursuant to normal agricultural practices with a setback of 10 m (30 ft) or greater from all property lines that does not change the direction, rate or quality of runoff resulting in a detrimental impact on neighbouring property'. By-law 41-2010 is a prohibition-only by-law for Schedule B lands with no standalone Site Alteration permit or fee (verified across all 17 pages of 2026 User Fees By-law No. 25-2026); non-exempt Schedule B work requires Council authorization via a Site Plan Agreement under s. 2 (2026 By-law 25-2026 pp. 10–11: Minor = $950.00 + HST; Major = 5% of site work cost, min $2,000.00 to max $6,400.00 + HST) or written exemption from Council under s. 4(o). No geographic fill origin ban.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: User Fee By-law 380-2003 (2026 Consolidation, Sched D p. 54 & Sched E p. 58 as replaced by By-law 163-2026); Site Alteration By-law 119-2024 (s. 4.1(9), Sched 1)
fields.security_deposit_terms: Non-exempt commercial reference (By-law 119-2024 Sched 2 s. 3.1(4) & Sched 4 s. 1.3(7)): Refundable security deposit / Financial Assurance in form and amount determined by Commissioner under Permit or Large Scale Site Alteration Agreement.
fields.peer_review_recovery: Non-exempt commercial reference (By-law 119-2024 Sched 4 s. 1.3(6)(c)): Owner reimburses City costs for administration, road repairs, and engagement of lawyers, engineers, hydrologists, environmental consultants, arborists, peer review, QC/QA, sampling, borehole testing, and compliance review.
fields.fee_formula_notes: VERIFIED FULL UNCAPPED NFP EXEMPTION ($0): Site Alteration By-law 119-2024 (Office Consolidation amended by 99-2025 & 129-2026; https://www.brampton.ca/EN/City-Hall/Bylaws/All%20Bylaws/Site%20Alteration%20By-law.pdf) s. 4.1(9) (pp. 9-10) provides a full uncapped exemption for Site Alterations 'incidental to a normal farm practice including such removal/placement as an incidental part of sod-farming, greenhouse operations, and nurseries for horticultural products' (subject to stockpile conditions: continuous use, restoration when suspended, <=6 months unchanged, no topsoil removal for sale). No out-of-municipality fill ban. 2026 Commercial Reference Schedule (User Fee By-law 380-2003 Sched D/E as replaced by By-law 163-2026 & By-law 119-2024 Sched 1 p. 26, HST exempt): Small Scale (<1,000 m³ on <=1 ha in 12 months) $450.00 flat ($225.00 renewal); Large Scale (>=1,000 m³ in 12 months, requiring Council approval, Public Meeting, and Site Alteration Agreement on title) $1,800.00 ($900.00 renewal) + $1.00/m³ Tipping Fee.

fields.security_deposit_terms: Letter of Credit of $2.00/m³ to secure compliance with Fill Permit conditions (Fill By-law 2007-59 s. 7(11), added by 2015-089), plus Public Works & Engineering road-damage securities (s. 7(7)).
fields.peer_review_recovery: No percentage peer-review chargeback in Fill By-law 2007-59; applicant must fund OLS certified site plan (s. 7(3)) and Qualified Person EPA contaminant certification for fill imported from outside Caledon (s. 7(9)); officer may retain experts during inspection (s. 20(2)(d)); Town remediation at owner's expense (s. 24).
fields.fee_formula_notes: MAJOR LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes based on unverified 'town policy'): Enacted Fill By-law 2007-59 (Office Consolidation amended through 2022-067 and 2026-066 eff. June 23, 2026; https://www.caledon.ca/assets/2026-07/Doc_637203057426383973%2027.pdf) contains NO agricultural or Normal Farm Practice permit exemption in Section 17 (which covers only <=150 mm lawn/garden dressing, demolition backfill, underground services, and executed development grading agreements). Instead, s. 11(1)(a) (added by 2015-089, p. 6) requires a Fill Permit for A-1/A-2/A-3 active agricultural lands demonstrating improved agricultural viability/productivity AND strictly prohibits permits exceeding 10,000 m³ ('The amount of fill to be imported onto the property does not exceed 10,000 cubic metres'; thus 15,000 m³ exceeds the statutory agricultural permit ceiling and evaluates to null). 2026 User Fees By-law 2025-105 Schedule C (p. 12 / PDF p. 15, HST exempt): <=500 m³ = $983.00 + $2.05/m³ ($2,008.00 at 500 m³); >500 m³ up to 10,000 m³ = $983.00 + $3.85/m³ ($20,233.00 at 5,000 m³). Note: Schedule C waives the $2.05/m³ component ONLY for topsoil fill relating to sod-farm operations, greenhouses, and horticultural nurseries (not general crop/livestock farms). Permit extension (>1 yr) $492.00; after-work-started surcharge $348.67; Heavy Truck Load Road Use (Sched K p. 46) $750 + $2.71/load/lane-km. Out-of-Town fill allowed with QP EPA certification (s. 7(9)). Replacement Site Alteration By-law under public consultation (May 2026), not yet enacted.

fields.fees_bylaw_name: 2026 Fee By-law (Final — Schedule 'C' 2026 Building & Planning, Site Alteration, p. 7) & Site Alteration By-law No. 72-2018 (enacted Aug 28, 2018, s. 4.1(h))

fields.fees_bylaw_name: Fees and Charges By-law 2026-07, Schedule D - Public Works Department; Site Alteration Fill By-law 2019-84 (ss. 3.1, 5.2, 6.1.5.5, 7.1, 12)
fields.security_deposit_terms: Cash, certified cheque, or irrevocable LOC (60 days' expiry notice) in amount set at Township's sole discretion up to 100% of estimated cost to maintain Site control measures, stabilize Site, and complete works; top-up within 30 days; plus road maintenance costs and Initial Road Condition Report (By-law 2019-84 ss. 12.8-12.15).
fields.peer_review_recovery: All Township legal, planning, administrative (Public Works), peer review consultant, engineering, soil testing, hydrogeology, environmental, and landscape costs + 10% administrative fee + 15%/yr interest (1.25%/mo) recovered from Owner or added to tax roll (By-law 2019-84 s. 12.4; 2026-07 Sched D).
fields.fee_formula_notes: MAJOR LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes via truncated excerpt): Visually verified Site Alteration Fill By-law 2019-84 (passed Dec 18, 2019; scanned 26-page PDF) s. 3.1 prohibits ALL Site Alteration unless in s. 4 or s. 5. Section 5.1 ONLY exempts topsoil removal. Section 5.2 & s. 7.1 allow a Bona Fide Farmer to place/dump fill >100 m³ up to a HARD ANNUAL LIMIT OF 1,000 m³ ONLY IF the farmer applies for and is granted a Permit (s. 5.2.1), submits a professional survey + P.Eng. submission (s. 5.2.2), agrees to the 1,000 m³/yr cap (s. 5.2.3), and submits a Certified Agrologist report at farmer's sole expense (s. 5.2.4)! Imports >1,000 m³/yr are PROHIBITED (so 5,000 m³ and 15,000 m³ safely evaluate to null!). Furthermore, s. 6.1.5.5 prohibits permitted Site Alteration on Class 1, 2, or 3 agricultural lands or specialty crop areas! 2026 Fees and Charges By-law 2026-07 Schedule D (Public Works): 'Fill up to 1000m³' = $250.00 + $2.00/m³ ($1,250.00 at 500 m³). Inspection $500; Approval/Exemption Renewal $250 (Expired $500); Special fine $10/m³ excess/unpermitted fill ($100/m³ if exceeding Table 2, s. 11.8).

fields.fees_bylaw_name: User Fees & Charges By-law 057-24, Schedule J - Engineering Services (s. 10.13, p. 40, Eff. Jan 1, 2026); Site Alteration By-law 108-23 (ss. 1.3.3(h), 3.1.2, 3.3)

fields.fee_formula_notes: MAJOR LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes): Enacted Site Alteration By-law 108-23 (passed Nov 22, 2023; https://www.innisfil.ca/media/file/site-alteration-by-law) s. 1.3.3(h) (p. 4) exempts Normal Farm Practice ONLY 'as so determined by the Normal Farm Practices Protection Board' (no automatic municipal $0 farm exemption!). Under s. 3.3 (p. 15, Bona Fide Farmer Permit), a non-exempt bona fide farmer placing/dumping fill >100 m³ [printed '1,00 m3'] must obtain a Permit, submit a professional survey + P.Eng. submission + Certified Agrologist report at sole expense, and agree to a 1,000 m³/yr annual cap (above 1,000 m³/yr requires standard commercial Medium/Large Permit & Council Approval/Agreement at >=5,000 m³ under s. 3.1.2). 2026 User Fees & Charges By-law 057-24 Schedule J s. 10.13 (p. 40, Eff. Jan 1, 2026, + HST): Minor (<150 m³, if required by Engineer per s. 3.1.6; s. 3.1.2 table lists <150 m³ Other as Permit Not Required) $2.70/m³; Small (150 to <1,500 m³) $1,060.90 flat ($1,060.90 at 500 m³); Medium (1,500 to <5,000 m³) $2,652.30 flat; Large (>=5,000 m³) $4,774.10 flat ($4,774.10 at 5,000 & 15,000 m³). Separate line item 10.13(e) Legal-Enforcement Matters: $0.50/m³ (+ HST); Renewal 50%; Violation 2x application fees.

fields.fee_formula_notes: MAJOR LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes without cap or origin restriction): Site Alteration By-law 2016-056 as amended by By-law 2017-046 s. 2 (https://portal.laserfiche.ca/Portal/DocView.aspx?id=45374&repo=r-000184d30821) replaces s. 3.2.6 to exempt fill placement incidental to normal farming practices (sod-farming/greenhouses/nurseries and improving site drainage/soil quality) ONLY UP TO 500 m³/year (s. 3.2.6.3) AND ONLY IF 'the source of the fill originates within the Township and complies with section 4.5.20' (s. 3.2.6.6 — out_of_muni_fill_ban = Restricted; fill imported from outside Oro-Medonte loses the 500 m³ exemption and requires a permit even at 500 m³, costing $750.00!). Director may still require a QP soils report (s. 3.3). Exhaustive review of 2026 Fees and Charges By-law 2025-129 (eff. Jan 1, 2026; Laserfiche id=1738592) confirms it contains NO general fill/volumetric site alteration fees (only Planning Table 1.1 Item 2.21 Residential <10 Units at $3,445.00), so Schedule A of By-law 2016-056 remains the governing fill fee schedule: <1,000 m³ = $500.00 + $0.50/m³ (Extension $250); >1,000 m³ (Council approval + registered agreement on title ss. 4.6.5/6.1/7.1) = $750.00 + $0.50/m³ (Extension $375; $3,250.00 at 5,000 m³; $8,250.00 at 15,000 m³). Unpermitted work = double fees + $250/inspection (s. 5.6).

Engineering Site Inspection $299.50; Renewal $119.80/$599.00/$1,198.00; Violation = 100% of applicable Application + Municipal Service Fees.

fields.security_deposit_terms: Amount determined by Director in sole discretion (cash or LOC with 30 days' expiry notice); interest accrues to Town; released only after Qualified Person written certification that Site Alteration meets applicable site condition standards (By-law 2016-58 Schedule A, p. 15).
fields.peer_review_recovery: No separate peer-review percentage surcharge in By-law 2016-58; applicant must retain a Qualified Person at own expense for Site Alteration Plan, SWMP, ESC Plan, fertility certificate (s. 5.6), and Soil Management Plan per Source Material Site (s. 7.2(m)). Emergency Town work: min $1,208.59 or actual cost + 15% admin + HST.
fields.fee_formula_notes: LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes): Site Alteration By-law 2016-58 (enacted Nov 14, 2016; https://www.newmarket.ca/media/file/2016-58-site-alteration-law, visually verified scanned PDF) s. 6.2 (p. 8) ONLY exempts 'Routine agricultural activity such as tilling, planting, harvesting and associated activities. Other agricultural activities are not exempt including activities such as construction of structures', and s. 6.12 (p. 9) ONLY exempts topsoil removal (not import). Importing/placing fill or topsoil >5 m³ (s. 6.16) on parcels >=0.5 ha (s. 6.3) requires a Site Alteration Permit PLUS a Qualified Person certificate confirming the Site Alteration will maintain or improve overall agricultural fertility (s. 5.6, p. 7). 2026 Schedule D Engineering Services (eff. Jan 1, 2026) sets Site Alteration Permit fees at: Owner Occupied Residential $304.27 (no HST); All Other Types of Property (including Agricultural): $2,260.98 (no HST; up 2% from $2,216.65 in 2025) PLUS Engineering Fees based on a percentage of the cost estimate of the works (+ HST). Because the variable Engineering Fee depends on project construction cost rather than m³ volume, volumetric benchmarks return null rather than understating total cost.

fields.fee_formula_notes: LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (flagged EX=Yes): Enacted Site Alteration By-law 47-25 (passed May 14, 2025, repealing 166-07; Municipal Code Ch. 967; https://www.richmondhill.ca/en/shared-content/resources/documents/Site-Alteration-Permit/47-25.pdf) Article 3 s. 3.1(c) (p. 7) and Schedule A Item 3 (p. 16) ONLY exempt 'the removal of topsoil as an incidental part of a normal agricultural practice including such removal as an incidental part of sod-farming, greenhouse operations and nurseries for horticultural products' (tracking Municipal Act s. 142(6)). Importing or placing fill/topsoil on agricultural lands is NOT exempt and requires a Site Alteration Permit (Schedule B.6 Excavate, Filling or Landscaping). Visually verified 2026 Tariff of Fees By-law 61-25 (eff. Jan 1, 2026, Schedule I p. 66): Item 4.vii 'Site Alteration Permit - Fill' = $656.00 flat per permit (HST: N; up from $643.00 in 2025). No volume tiers or per-m³ fee.

fields.fee_formula_notes: LEGACY DB DISCREPANCY (legacy DB cited repealed Fill By-law 189-96 s. 2(1)(h)): Site Alteration By-law 031-2024 (eff. Feb 21, 2024; https://www.vaughan.ca/sites/default/files/2024-02/031-2024.pdf) repealed the broader agricultural fill-placement exemption in 189-96 and narrowed s. 6.0(1)(j) (p. 12) strictly to 'the Removal or replacement of Topsoil from Agricultural Lands as part of Normal Farm Practice such as Sod-farming, greenhouse operations and nurseries for horticultural productions' (excluding topsoil removal for sale/exchange). General fill / excess soil import onto agricultural land is NOT broadly exempt, requires proof that the Site Alteration maintains or improves overall agricultural fertility (s. 5.0(4)(a), p. 10), and triggers Fees and Charges By-law 051-2026 Schedule K (pp. 35-36, eff. Feb 24, 2026): Excess Soil Import (Receiving Site) = $11,033.00 flat (HST exempt; same $11,033.00 flat for Cut & Fill Operation, Excess Soil Export, and Non-Development storage; 2027 rate also $11,033.00). Note: Narrow topsoil replacement specifically qualifying under s. 6.0(1)(j) (e.g., sod farms/greenhouses/nurseries replacing topsoil as NFP) remains permit-exempt ($0). Renewal/Amendment 50% of permit fee; Non-compliance inspection $353 (2026)/$364 (2027); Compliance Order Appeal $309 (2026)/$318 (2027); Special fine $10/m³ unpermitted fill ($100/m³ if exceeding Table 2, s. 10.0(3)).

fields.fee_formula_notes: VERIFIED AG EXEMPT ($0) FOR TOPSOIL SPREADING <=200 MM (NO m³ CAP): Site Alteration By-law 2024-037-RE (passed Apr 24, 2024, repealing 2019-068-RE; https://whitchurch.civicweb.net/document/184502/, visually verified scanned PDF) s. 3.1(n) (p. 7) exempts 'Site Alterations that are directly related to a Normal Farm Practice that is legally established under the Town's Zoning By-law, including the application of Topsoil for spreading over Agricultural Property provided that the Existing Grade of the Property is not increased by more than two hundred (200) millimetres' (active FRFOFA/FBRN registration in good standing required; no m³ volume cap).
